records.name: pregenesis-grammar
records.summary: The Pre-Genesis host grammar declares the inscription alphabet {<, >, a, b} and three public starts: ground_token (exactly <>), inscription (one balanced, non-nested bracketed inscription) and pre_genesis_regime (zero or more inscriptions between braces, where {} is host list notation and not the empty word). It keeps four states apart: absent input, the empty word, the literal token <> and the ground carrier that S(0) adopts. It has no event productions: the first event, supply(<>), is the Genesis boundary, and parsing a word admits no carrier, transition or observational operation.
records.obligation: Parse Pre-Genesis words with the declared grammar only, refuse the empty word at every public start, and admit nothing by parsing; supply(<>) belongs to Genesis.
imports: Declared host grammar pre_genesis.ebnf, a later host notation not tested by the model trials (assumption)
records.fence: A grammar verdict is a syntax check of host notation; it assigns no semantics to <> and does not decide whether an inscription is admitted.

records.name: repetition-needs-structure
records.summary: To tell 'the inscription remains' from 'a second occurrence has been produced', a regime needs at least two stages or positions, an identity criterion across them, a copying or persistence rule and a stable alphabet: repetition is succession plus retained identity. Trial 2's proposed step <> → <> therefore already carries structure, the self-loop id_<> : <> → <>, and is not a free primitive. The first generated operation may then be identity, persistence or reproduction rather than a new payload such as <a>. The source labels this an analysis of what the word 'repeat' presupposes, not a proof.
records.obligation: Treat a proposed repetition of <> as requiring declared positions, a cross-position identity criterion, a persistence rule and a stable alphabet, and record a self-loop as added structure, not as the absence of a step.
records.fence: Conceptual analysis with no proof; it does not show that repetition is the canonical first operation, and Genesis does not adopt a repetition rule from it.

records.name: presentation-not-expressive-lift
records.summary: Write P for the presented inscriptions and O for the internal observations. Supplying <a> after <> changes P from {<>} to {<a>} and leaves O_1 = O_0 = ∅, so no new internal distinction is available. With q : P → N sending an inscription to the distinctions the regime has, x ≠ y in P can hold while q(x) = q(y) in N, so a new presentation does not imply a new internal class, and in the other direction q(x) = q(y) does not imply x = y. Under the opaque convention <a> is a new presentation state in the same internal class as <>; the statement holds under that convention only.
records.obligation: Keep the presentation P and the internal quotient N as separate records, so that supplying <a> with O empty adds a presentation state and no internal class, and never infer x = y from q(x) = q(y).
imports: Opaque identity convention: a state is what the regime can tell apart, so internal identity is the quotient by ≈ₙ (assumption)

records.name: forced-separation-lift-not-unique
records.summary: Suppose an external task requires <a> and <ab> to differ while the current regime has <a> ≈ₙ <ab>. Every operation f on the quotient S_n/≈ₙ gives f([<a>]) = f([<ab>]), so no operation on the current quotient answers the task on every input, and a refinement adding at least one observation o with o(<a>) ≠ o(<ab>) is forced; the analysis gives this as an argument with proof. records.name: replay-necessity
records.summary: Let H be the possible histories, σ(h) the state that history h produces and π(h) the part of h an auditor sees, for example only the last turn. If π(h₁) = π(h₂) but σ(h₁) ≠ σ(h₂), no auditor A that sees only π reports σ(h) for every h, because A(π(h₁)) = A(π(h₂)) would give σ(h₁) = σ(h₂). The trial failures motivate the theorem: the blind auditor flagged the licensed words 'We' (Trial 1) and 'rule' (Trial 2) as imports, so an audit needs two levels; in Trial 2, Prompt 14's false attribution was answered without objection, so claim provenance is a check separate from claim correctness, Result 15 lost the state, saying the regime contains only <> after <a> had been supplied; and the two-level auditor, shown only that turn, answered None. State certification therefore needs replay information that separates the relevant histories, and on a declared finite population a summary on which σ is constant per fiber of the view can stand in for the raw history.
records.obligation: Reject any auditor that certifies the adopted state from a view π under which two admissible histories with different states coincide, and give it the replayed history or a summary on which σ is constant per fiber.
records.fence: The trial contrasts motivate the theorem and do not instantiate it: the truncated window and the full replay received different inputs, so they are not a checked pair with equal auditor views; raw history retention is a provenance policy, and task-sufficient reconstruction is the mathematical requirement.
